_about: Anatomical review decisions per source mesh or per canonical structure. Only a named reviewer writes here; scripts never set a status other than `pending`. `scripts/validate-reviews.py` checks that every referenced id exists and that every shipped mesh has an entry or falls under the default.

default.reason: No anatomist has reviewed any mesh, landmark or registration yet.

known_issues.issue: Outlying geometry above the head in the source Toes segmentation (see generated/anatomy-qa.json outlier_components).
known_issues.action: Exclude the outlier components or the label from any future composite until reviewed; the label is not composed in 0.4.

known_issues.issue: CT sacrum label differs from the Denver sacrum by p95 about 10 mm and Hausdorff about 30 mm under the same-donor pelvis fit (coccyx and sacral extent).
known_issues.action: Denver sacrum is used in the composite; CT sacrum remains an alternative.

known_issues.issue: Head placement is a bounding-box fit into the CT brain envelope; cervical continuity unreviewed.
known_issues.action: Anatomist review of the skull base and cervical spine junction.

known_issues.issue: Lumbar numbering of the VHF donor: three CT models (TotalSegmentator, MOOSE, Skellytour) find six lumbar-type vertebral bodies between the last rib-bearing vertebra and the sacrum on both the NLM fresh CT (z 556 to 740) and the Denver aligned CT, and each forces five names onto them differently (generated/ct-prior-consensus-{nlm,denver}.json; L2 Dice 0.39, 0.19, 0.01 in the worst pairs). The shipped CT labels L1 to L3 are therefore unreliable in extent and name.
known_issues.action: Vertebra consensus works on geometric instances with neutral ids (scripts/ct-vertebra-instances.py, generated/ct-vertebra-instances-{nlm,denver}.json); L1 to L3 of nlm-vhf-ct stay marked as automatic and disputed. Numbering evidence gathered so far, in order of preference (plan B section 2.5): same-donor published references first, anatomist only for what they cannot close.

evidence.source: HRA united-female v1.5 skeleton (public/atlases/hra-female.json, assets VH_F_lumbar_vertebra_1..6, VH_F_thoracic_vertebra_1..12, seven cervical, VH_F_sacrum), modelled on the Visible Human Female
evidence.statement: 25 vertebrae: 7 cervical, 12 thoracic, 6 lumbar, plus a fused sacrum

evidence.source: NIH 3D entry 3DPX-020988, Spinal Cord, Female (HRA, CC BY 4.0, created 2024-03-06, published 2025-08-05)
evidence.statement: "The Visible Human Female has 6 lumbar vertebrae, and the total length of her spinal column is 60.923 cm."
evidence.limits: supports the count and the order; it does not validate our mask boundaries, nor say whether the body TotalSegmentator calls S1 (fused to the sacrum by MOOSE and Skellytour) is sacral or a lumbarised segment

known_issues.open_question: Lumbosacral transition: TotalSegmentator segments a separate S1 body (about 49 mL) under the sixth lumbar-type body; MOOSE labels it sacrum and Skellytour pelvis. Whether it is S1 of a normal sacrum below six lumbar vertebrae or a further transitional segment is not decided by any reference found so far.
